calas:Ayazma.group: The south coast, on a north wind

old.name: Ayazma
old.hook: The island's busiest beach — fine golden sand and turquoise water, loungers and a row of fish-and-meze restaurants for a sunset beer.
old.text: The island's busiest beach — fine golden sand and turquoise water, loungers and a row of fish-and-meze restaurants for a sunset beer. Named for the 1734 Aya Paraskevi monastery and its holy spring behind it ( ayazma = Greek hagiasma , holy water), which opens once a year on 26 July for the saint's-day pilgrimage. Best on a north (poyraz) wind; arrive before 10am in July–August or there is no sand left. Free + paid loungers, south coast · Open in Google Maps →

calas:Sulubahçe.group: The south coast, on a north wind

old.name: Sulubahçe
old.hook: Ayazma's quiet neighbour: the same crystal water and good sand, but no loungers and no café, so it keeps its natural character — and its campers.
old.text: Ayazma's quiet neighbour: the same crystal water and good sand, but no loungers and no café, so it keeps its natural character — and its campers. Rocky shelves at the eastern end draw snorkellers. Like Ayazma it wants a north wind and is exposed when the lodos turns. No facilities, bring everything · Open in Google Maps →

calas:Habbele.group: The south coast, on a north wind

old.name: Habbele (Poyraz Limanı)
old.hook: The closest swimmable cove to town and the family pick — a bowl-shaped bay so calm even a poyraz can't roughen it, the warmest, shallowest water on the island.
old.text: The closest swimmable cove to town and the family pick — a bowl-shaped bay so calm even a poyraz can't roughen it, the warmest, shallowest water on the island. Golden sand with a paid lounger section at one end and a free pitch-your-own stretch at the other. Watch for sea urchins on the bottom — wear water shoes. Free + paid, closest to town · Open in Google Maps →

calas:Akvaryum.group: East and west — clear water and the wind

old.name: Akvaryum (Aquarium Cove)
old.hook: An east-coast cove named for water so clear you can count the fish — the island's snorkelling spot, and the one that comes into its own on a south (lodos) wind.
old.text: An east-coast cove named for water so clear you can count the fish — the island's snorkelling spot, and the one that comes into its own on a south (lodos) wind. No sunbeds, showers or changing rooms; the access track is rough, so park at the roadside and walk the last fifteen minutes (or take the summer shuttle). Snorkelling, no facilities · Open in Google Maps →

calas:Çayır.group: East and west — clear water and the wind

old.name: Çayır
old.hook: The windy beach, deliberately — a flat, exposed north-side point that catches the full poyraz, which makes it the island's windsurf and kitesurf centre rather than a place to swim calm.
old.text: The windy beach, deliberately — a flat, exposed north-side point that catches the full poyraz, which makes it the island's windsurf and kitesurf centre rather than a place to swim calm. It hosted the European Kitesurf Championship in 2015 and has a kite school on site; the swimmers go elsewhere, the boards come here. Windsurf / kite, not calm swimming · Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Tuzburnu

old.text: A remote rocky cove at the western tip below the lighthouse and windmills, reachable only by car with no facilities at all.
